transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-06-13
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~72 minutes
Attendees: Liam O'Neill (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood CSM), Arjun Patel (Redwood SE), Nina Hart (Cobalt Bridge VP Eng), Rajiv Menon (Platform Eng), Sophie Alvarez (Security Lead), Ben Carter (DevOps)

Auto-generated topics (may be imperfect):
- VPC onboarding and private deployment steps
- Access, creds, and sandbox provisioning
- Security checklist: SOC2, KMS, SSO, audit logs
- Staging load test and success criteria

Transcript body:
[00:00] Liam: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call, uh, we'll run about an hour, hour fifteen, right. Maya, Arjun with me.
[00:07] Maya: hi all.
[00:09] Nina: Hey, thanks, yes this is Nina.
[00:11] Rajiv: Rajiv here.
[00:12] Sophie: Sophie.
[00:13] Ben: Ben, on audio.
[00:16] Liam: Cool. Goal today is to get you into a Redwood Dedicated staging — like a sandbox that mirrors your prod-ish networking — and align on security items so the legal team doesn't come back with surprise asks. We'll also schedule a hands-on load smoke next week.
[00:31] Rajiv: Sounds good. For context, our infra is GCP, we run k8s, private GKE with VPC peering. We will want the Dedicated instance in our VPC, or at least peered.
[00:41] Arjun: Right, we support VPC peering and private deployments — Redwood Private — and for Dedicated we can do VPC peering or private link depending on the cloud. Slight note: sometimes the auto-provisioned routes need a quick route table tweak.
[00:55] Nina: Ok, our main asks: SSO + SAML early, KMS integration for keys, and logs retention for 12 months. Also low latency target: API p95 < 200ms for short completions.
[01:09] Liam: Got it. We'll surface the SSO flow — we have a SAML connector and can do SCIM for user provisioning. KMS — we integrate with customer-managed KMS/HSMs but there are a few options depending on Dedicated vs Private.
[01:22] Sophie: A quick question: for KMS, is that envelope encryption only or do you hold any customer keys? We need to ensure keys never leave our control.
[01:30] Maya: short answer: customer-managed keys, we do not keep plaintext. But Arjun will go through the HSM handshake and key wrapping.
[01:37] Arjun: Yep. For Dedicated we can configure a key-wrap model where you maintain the master key in your KMS, Redwood gets wrapped keys only. There was one case where the phrasing in the security form was confusing — we call it key wrap and the paperwork says K M S, sometimes shows up as K V cache in notes — so apologies for the transcription noise.
[01:57] Ben: ha, KV cache is something else, but yes. On networking: we will only allow egress to specific IPs, and we manage NAT. Will you provide an allowlist for the sandbox?
[02:07] Liam: Yes. We'll send an allowlist and temporary IPs for the Dedicated sandbox. Those IPs might change when we move to reserved production IPs but we'll mark them.
[02:14] Nina: Great. On the SLOs: the <200ms figure is for 256-token completions, approximate. We also have burst throughput needs — about 20 qps sustained for our search reranker workload.
[02:27] Arjun: Understood. For the staging run we'll configure a model similar to your target topology — quantized variant for cost tradeoffs — but we can also run the unquantized baseline if you prefer.
[02:38] Rajiv: Can you explain the tradeoffs again? Quantized models cost less but do we lose quality?
[02:43] Arjun: There's usually a small delta. Our Redwood Optimize engine gives recommendations — we can run the same eval prompt set and show token-level quality metrics. For reranking, that's often fine.
[02:55] Liam: And just to flag: if you need fallback behaviour we can configure automatic fallback to a slightly cheaper model variant, and we expose metrics in the console.
[03:03] Sophie: about audit logs — do you store full request payloads? Our compliance needs say we must have full request/response logging for a rolling 12 months, and we need to know encryption at rest.
[03:14] Maya: We can retain logs to 12 months as an add-on. For request payloads we support redaction rules and token-level cost indexing. We'll share the security docs that explain encryption at rest (AES-256), in transit (TLS1.2/1.3), and retention options.
[03:30] Ben: Also need a note on PII handling. If a user uploads documents to an ingest pipeline, we need to ensure those vectors or embeddings are not retained in a way that violates regs. What's Redwood's stance?
[03:41] Liam: By default hosted models are ephemeral but for Dedicated in your VPC we can control retention policy and purge windows. We'll document the default behaviour and the options for immediate deletion post-processing.
[03:52] Nina: Good. Next, creds: for the sandbox, what's the preferred auth? API keys? SSO?
[03:58] Arjun: For early sandbox we typically create service credentials scoped to a sandbox project — API key or short-lived token. For human access to console we use SAML SSO. For the hands-on test we can create a timeboxed API key you can rotate later.
[04:12] Rajiv: Sounds fine. Can we get a list of the endpoints and a quick curl example? Our devs like those.
[04:18] Liam: We'll include a quickstart curl and Postman collection in the onboarding bundle.
[04:22] Maya: I'll also create a sprint calendar in the workspace and invite your team, with milestones for security review, staging run, and go/no-go.
[04:31] (short pause)
[04:35] Sophie: One more security Q — is there a way to keep audit logs in our own Splunk or SIEM? We prefer pushing logs to our Splunk instance.
[04:43] Arjun: yes we support push via syslog or cloud logging export for GCP. We can set up a sink to your logging project, and you can ingest it into Splunk. There are a few minor field mapping items we document.
[04:58] Ben: ok, good. On routing: we will need region affinity — traffic must stay in eu-west1 for EU customers. Will that be supported in Dedicated?
[05:07] Liam: Yes, you can pin regions and we also support routing policies to prefer eu-west1 with fallbacks. We'll note that cross-region fallback can be disabled if you need strict residency.
[05:19] Rajiv: timeline question — we want a pilot in staging within two weeks, and a production pilot in four weeks. Is that realistic?
[05:26] Maya: Two-week staging run is tight but doable if we get your access and test prompts this week.
[05:32] Nina: We'll aim to get the prompts and compliance checklist by Thursday.
[05:36] Liam: Great. Next I'm going to hand over to Arjun for a quick run-through of the onboarding playbook and the sandbox provisioning steps.
[05:44] Arjun: Cool. I work through a checklist: 1) Network allowlist and peering config; 2) Service account and API key provisioning; 3) KMS wrapping config; 4) SSO/SAML for console; 5) Test dataset and prompts for quality tests; 6) Load test scenario and expected metrics. For the sandbox I'll provision a small Dedicated pool — two GPUs equivalent — to run the smoke.
[06:10] Nina: Two GPUs ok. For the reranker workload we'll simulate QPS and a concurrent KV cache usage pattern — hope that small pool will still show latency trends.
[06:20] Arjun: Should be fine for p95 signals; throughput scaling we can emulate with synthetic clients.
[06:26] (crosstalk)
[06:28] Sophie: Another compliance note: we need a data processing agreement and a subprocessor list. Does Redwood provide that?
[06:35] Liam: Yes, we have a DPA and subprocessor addendum. I'll attach both to the deck I send.
[06:40] Ben: Any IP addresses for the sandbox so we can start firewall rules?
[06:44] Liam: We'll provide a temporary allowlist in the next email. Note those IPs are for sandbox and may change. If you need static production IPs we can discuss reserved capacity.
[06:55] Rajiv: ok. Let's talk about the staging smoke: what are the success criteria?
[07:00] Maya: We usually define success as: 1) connectivity verified (SAML + API), 2) p95 latency within target band, 3) no unexpected errors above 1% error rate, 4) logs flowing into your SIEM, and 5) a basic quality check where reranker accuracy meets baseline.
[07:17] Nina: good. For the quality baseline we'll give you 500 sample prompts and expected top-3 reranker results.
[07:24] Arjun: Perfect. We'll run evaluation and produce a small report comparing tokens, latency, and model deltas.
[07:30] (15-second silence)
[07:46] Ben: On the topic of pricing for the pilot — is the staging discounted or usage free?
[07:52] Liam: For early pilots we often provide credits for staging and an evaluation credit. Production pricing will be usage-based with options for reserved Dedicated commits. We'll include a pilot pricing line in the follow-up email.
[08:04] Sophie: If we decide to run private deployment on-prem later, any difference in the KMS flow?
[08:09] Arjun: On-prem is similar but we provide an on-prem package and you keep the keys locally. There are differences in network and ops responsibilities; we'll document an ops runbook for that scenario.
[08:22] Rajiv: any gotchas with Kubernetes or the kube-proxy?
[08:26] Arjun: sometimes MTU or route table mismatches cause slow connections; we include a connectivity script in the onboarding bundle to validate peering.
[08:36] Nina: ok. Let's capture milestones and owners.
[08:39] Maya: I'll put together a one-week sprint: Day 1 access and allowlist, Day 2 SSO/creds, Day 3 KMS handshake, Day 4 run smoke, Day 5 produce report.
[08:51] Ben: That helps. For the smoke we'll schedule a 30–45 minute session where Redwood runs the scripts with us observing.
[08:59] Liam: We'll do that.
[09:02] (longer exchange detailing specific ports and sample curl flows, trimmed by transcript)
[10:12] (approx) Arjun: Example curl: curl -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.internal/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -d '{"prompt":"<sample>", "max_tokens":64}' — we'll supply exact endpoints in the docs (note: transcript may show slight hostname mismatch).
[10:30] Sophie: Fine. One more ask — we want to validate the KV cache behavior for chat-like sessions; do you have tooling to replay conversation prefixes?
[10:39] Arjun: Yes, we can replay sessions against the same model kernel to validate KV cache hit rates, and show savings on token cost. We'll include those scripts.
[10:50] Nina: Great. Anything else?
[10:53] Liam: Quick recap then next steps. Recap: Redwood to send security deck, onboarding bundle (curl examples, allowlist, syslog config), and create sandbox Dedicated with temporary creds. Cobalt Bridge to send prompts, compliance checklist, and confirm egress/firewall rules. We'll schedule the hands-on smoke next week.
[11:11] Nina: Sounds good.
[11:13] Ben: good.
[11:15] Sophie: thanks.
[11:16] Maya: I'll send calendar invites and the sprint write-up by end of day tomorrow.
[11:21] Liam: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email and post the artifacts in the shared drive.
[11:26] (meeting winding down, small talk)
[11:45] END
